subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should command-lane aging preserve fresh foreground/user priority over every aged lower-priority class, including normal/default, or may aged normal/default work tie or overtake foreground after the threshold?
rationale: The linked issue asks for a starvation guard, but the permanent scheduler contract changes existing session ordering and affects interactive latency under load.

options.title: Repair foreground-preserving aging
options.body: Keep fresh foreground/user work strictly higher than aged normal/default and background work, add the missing regression, and update comments and proof to match.

options.title: Choose stronger anti-starvation
options.body: Allow aged lower-priority work to tie or overtake foreground after the threshold, but make that tradeoff explicit in the PR body, comments, tests, and related issue triage.

options.title: Defer to broader scheduler design
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want aging, foreground reserve, and gateway fairness policy to land as one coordinated scheduler design.

recommendation.title: Repair foreground-preserving aging
recommendation.body: Keep fresh foreground/user work strictly higher than aged normal/default and background work, add the missing regression, and update comments and proof to match.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has original queue history and authored the overlapping priority/starvation scheduler proposal, making him the best available owner for the policy choice.
